'''Hell''' is the name [[Matcha Flavoured]] gives to {{MCW|The Nether|the Nether}}. The pack renames the dimension's blocks and items to match: netherrack is [[Hellstone]], Nether bricks are [[Hellbricks]], Nether wart is [[Hellspore]], Nether gold ore is [[Gilded Hellstone]] and Nether quartz ore is [[Sulfurous Hellstone]]. Entering it grants the advancement "Orpheus" ("Descend into Hell").

In the pack's progression, Hell is where [[Blessing]]s and [[Hell-Bound Book]]s are made from stolen prayers, and where [[adamant scrap]] is found in [[Bastion Remnant]]s. The [[Wither effect]] is especially dangerous there, and the release notes urge players to "bring milk or bread to Hell".

== Environment ==
The pack overrides Hell's dimension type:<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/dimension_type/the_nether.json}}</ref>
{| class="wikitable"
! Property !! Matcha Flavoured !! Vanilla
|-
| Ambient light || 0.3 || 0.1
|-
| Fog start distance || 0 blocks || 10 blocks
|-
| Fog end distance || 300 blocks || 96 blocks
|-
| Water evaporates || No || Yes
|}
The higher ambient light makes dark areas less dark, while the fog starts at the player and reaches much farther.

=== Water ===
{{Diagram|Hell water|align=right|width=360|caption=Emptying a water bucket below the roof clears all water within 20 blocks of the player; on the roof, water stays.}}
Although the dimension type no longer evaporates water, water cannot be kept inside Hell. Whenever a player empties a water bucket while in Hell between Y=0 and Y=127, the pack removes all water in a cube reaching 20 blocks from the player in every direction. The fill covers more blocks than the vanilla limit for one command, but the pack raises the <code>max_block_modifications</code> game rule to 200,000, so it succeeds.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/setup/gamerules.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/nether_water.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/predicate/invalid_nether_water.json}}</ref> Water can be placed on the Nether roof (Y=128 and above). The 1.10 release notes explain the rule: "Guys please I just want flowers in the nether stop being naughty".<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.10|quote=Water can no longer be placed *inside* of Hell (Guys please I just want flowers in the nether stop being naughty)}}</ref>

== Generation ==
* '''No gravel''': the Hell noise settings no longer place gravel on the surface of Nether Wastes, Soul Sand Valleys and Basalt Deltas, and the <code>ore_gravel_nether</code> feature is removed from Nether Wastes, Soul Sand Valleys, Crimson Forests and Warped Forests.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/worldgen/noise_settings/nether.json}}</ref>
* '''Hellspore''': patches of [[Hellspore]] at random growth stages generate on soul sand in Nether Wastes and Soul Sand Valleys.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/worldgen/placed_feature/nether_wart.json}}</ref>
* Soul Sand Valleys have a darker fog (<code>#061919</code>) and sky (<code>#030d0d</code>). Crimson Forests have fewer floating spores, and Warped Forests have a pale blue fog (<code>#a2b5dd</code>). See [[Biomes#Changes by biome]].

== Trivia ==
* "Hell is too dark" was one of the most common complaints. The developer agreed only in part, saying they like dark Nethers and treating it as a matter of taste; the 1.12 increase in ambient light was a compromise.<ref>{{Cite video|id=wavOi0ULYpQ|title=How Criticism changed Matcha Flavoured|quote=a big complaint that I've been getting is that the Nether is too dark. And I completely understand why people think that and I agree with it to a degree. However, I really like dark nethers.}}</ref>
